newsitem.title: UK: UK share trader fined for misinforming clients.
newsitem.headline: UK share trader fined for misinforming clients.

text.p: Share dealer City Equities Ltd has been fined 250,000 pounds ($408,000) for misinforming clients on the risks of trading in so-called "penny shares", a British investment watchdog said on Monday.
City Equities must also pay 30,906 pounds for costs of the inquiry into its dealings by the Financial Intermediaries, Managers and Brokers Regulatory Association (FIMBRA).

City Equities admitted charges that it did not explain the risks of investing in cheap shares, that it made unsolicited calls to try to conclude deals over the phone and that it failed to establish whether its recommendations suited clients, FIMBRA said.
It also found that City Equities failed to keep proper records or maintain staff supervision procedures.
The enquiry into City Equities practices followed a routine compliance visit by FIMBRA earlier this year. ($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
